source.title: Unlearning Is Not Just Erasing: Temporal Decoupling via Generation Inequality
source.authors: Xun-Lei Chen; Qi-Rui Ye; Yuang Li; Yi-Fan Gong; Zhao-Kun Wang; WenYi Li; Shiyao Guo; Jin-Yu Guo

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the main paper through its references, but not the appendices it cites for additional analyses and details.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests recovery and robustness using its own pathway-contribution replacement interventions and altered-prompt attacks, rather than reproducing the original methods or attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports internal contribution replacement results and prompt-scaffolding/adaptive-recovery results. It does not test recovery through fine-tuning, quantization, or prompt rephrasing alone. Baseline-method results are not treated as attacks or recovery tests.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a new unlearning method (ADU) and reports three kinds of evidence. WMDP forgetting and retention results bear on A. Patching Base contributions back into ADU's selected attention edges restores much of the suppressed WMDP accuracy, which bears on C. Six prompt-based attacks bear on E and F, but their results appear only in a figure. Version labels in the record were V1/V3/V5/V6; they map to A/C/E/F.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors also present ADU as a persistent parameter-level mechanism that limits recovery under altered prompts. They note stronger guarantees against residual knowledge recovery as future work, which implicitly concedes that access is suppressed rather than the knowledge being erased.
record.recipe_differences: ADU trains attention-projection adapters to suppress fixed preplan–anchor pathways; the tested recovery intervention replaces selected edge contributions rather than applying fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, or quantization.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that selection ratio q and loss balance α alter the forgetting–retention trade-off; larger q can include benign anchors and harm retention, and larger α can reduce retention. The text gives no attack-result numbers for these sensitivities.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing the selected preplan–anchor edge contributions from the Base model lowers WMDP accuracy 58.62→36.37; matched-random removal gives 57.09.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Specific attention pathways mediate retrieval of hazardous knowledge in the original model.

record.problems: The robustness results in Figure 5 are not numerically transcribed in the text. The supplied text lacks the cited appendices, and the recovery intervention is reported for one model and WMDP average accuracy. The paper does not provide a never-trained comparator or state a chance-level reference for the WMDP scores.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for other benchmark metrics unrelated to the recovery and retention measures recorded here. Appendix analyses are not present in the supplied text.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning or quantization attacks; no never-trained comparator.
No activation-direction ablation. The only internal edit patches in Base-model contributions.
No other-language or plain-rephrasing attacks. Attack magnitudes are not reported in text.
ADU's robustness is not tested against fine-tuning, quantization or activation ablation.

missing.what: Numerical worst-case attacked accuracies for ADU, ALU and ASU, plus Base, under both attack groups.
missing.locator: Figure 5; Appendix F.1 (not in supplied text)

missing.what: MMLU under the patching interventions (ADU←Base selected 63.37; matched random 61.64).
ADU forgetting results on MUSE-Harry Potter (Llama2-7B: BLEU 4.78 vs original 74.80, MMLU 45.64 vs 46.33) and TOFU (FQ 0.93).

record.verdict_notes: ADU trains only LoRA attention adapters on a frozen backbone, so by design it blocks retrieval routes. The C evidence shows this, but it uses Base-model activations rather than an adversary-available edit. The attack evidence is figure-only and limited to prompt attacks, so the E and F verdicts rest on the text's qualitative statements. The record used version labels V1/V3/V5/V6; these were remapped to A/C/E/F.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports ADU forgetting and retention results and altered-prompt attack results, but does not state a chance-level reference or compare recovery with a model that never learned the target knowledge.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning set is tested.
No single activation-direction ablation is reported; the intervention replaces selected pre-output-projection edge contributions.
The paper tests few-shot, masking, role-play CoT, anchor-shift, multi-turn probing, and repeated-sampling attacks, not other languages or rephrasing alone.
Robustness is tested for the paper's prompt-scaffolding and adaptive-recovery attack groups, not against fine-tuning or quantization.
